Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m starting with `README.md` as required. Then I’ll use the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill because this task changes a multi-wake dogfish target policy; its inspection order will guide the evidence review before any solver edit.

The skill requires anchoring the keyframes to observations and metrics, then comparing the strongest run with the most informative contrasting run. I’ll now inventory the workspace and read the parent guidance before inspecting those images; I will not use the omitted research shelf or any neighboring/history sources.

The common prewarm shows the held fish above and to the right of a fully developed four-street wake, confirming every policy starts from the same wake phase. In the released sheets, both the best run and slower contrast self-propel upstream into the wake and turn toward capture, but the best run follows a visibly shallower, faster approach and carries much lower lateral load. I’m cross-checking that difference against controller parameters and time-series metrics before writing the required hypothesis note.

The visual/metric cross-check changes the inherited conclusion: static steering is no longer monotonically better as gain rises. With the propulsion core fixed and the 10° limit fixed, gain `0.75` is the local best; `0.82` regresses arrival, mean distance, upstream-relative speed, joint excursion, and load. The skill now requires me to record that diagnosis and a falsifiable candidate hypothesis before touching the policy, so I’m doing that next.

The candidate is now a single one-axis interpolation: `steering_gain=0.77`, with the proven gait, 10° bound, and action guard unchanged. I also materially replaced the durable guidance’s prior monotonic-gain lesson with the new three-point bracket and its limit-expansion falsification boundary. Next I’m validating the schema and required guidance delta through the workspace’s mandated check runner; I will not run CFD.

The guidance check passed. The policy check did not actually run because the login-shell startup tried to configure a nonexistent workspace-local SSH path and then could not find `julia`; the wrapper misleadingly returned zero. I’m rerunning without login-shell startup to get a trustworthy result, then I’ll execute the separate boundary check.

The boundary check passed. The remaining lightweight Julia assertion is blocked by the cluster’s `juliaup` launcher trying—and failing—to fetch its release-channel database; this is an environment bootstrap issue, not a policy assertion. I’m checking the alternate installed launcher and the deterministic static schema guard so the handoff does not mistake the launcher failure for a candidate failure.

Final verification is clean for the workspace-controlled checks: material guidance/notes PASS, boundary PASS, and the deterministic `params.FIELD` schema guard PASS. Only the optional runtime Julia assertion could not launch because the cluster has no installed `juliaup` channel and its channel-database download is being reset; no CFD was attempted.

Implemented exactly one multi-wake candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1): isolated `steering_gain=0.77` interpolation near the sampled `0.75` optimum.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): visual diagnosis and falsifiable hypothesis.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:78): materially revised lesson showing the static-gain benefit turns over near `0.75`.

Checks:

- Guidance/material-update check: PASS
- Solver boundary check: PASS
- Deterministic parameter-schema guard: PASS
- Julia runtime assertion: unavailable because the cluster’s `juliaup` has no installed channel and its database download was reset.

No CFD was run.
